report_meta.system: Salesforce Services and Corporate Services Covered Services System

meta_quotes.quote: System and Organization Controls (SOC2) Type 2 ... Salesforce, Inc.'s Salesforce Services and Corporate Services Covered Services System ... For the Period November 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026
Ernst & Young LLP Suite 1600 560 Mission Street San Francisco, CA ... Independent Service Auditor’s Assurance Report To the Board of Directors of Salesforce, Inc.:

3.1.1.quote: SC-18 (SS): Encryption is used to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information being transmitted over the Internet between the Customer and Salesforce.
3.1.1.note: TLS is named ('Cryptographic keys for TLS certificates are monitored by the Security team for expiration.', p. 62) but no TLS version is stated anywhere, so no exact dropdown match.

3.1.2.detail: Encryption at rest confirmed; cipher/standard not named in report
3.1.2.quote: Encryption at Rest The Salesforce Services Covered Services offer multiple features for encryption of Customer Data at rest.
3.1.2.note: 'AES' does not appear anywhere in this report; the at-rest standard is not named. Shield Platform Encryption operations occur within a Hardware Security Module (p. 63).

3.1.3.detail: Backup encryption stated only for the Salesforce Backup and Recover Next product; no standard named
3.1.3.quote: Backup data is secured with encryption in transit and at rest, and the application provides activity logs for review and monitoring of backup, restore, and export activities.
3.1.3.note: This quote is from the description of the 'Salesforce Backup and Recover Next' covered service. The main Backup, Recovery, and System Availability section (p. 69) does not state encryption of backups for the core services.

3.1.4.quote: The customer’s Working Key, which encrypts the customer data fields, is stored in the core database after being encrypted (wrapped) by a Salesforce Managed Master Key.
3.1.4.note: Two-tier model: Salesforce-managed master key/secret plus customer-specific key material. Shield Platform Encryption: 'The DEK derivation utilizes a Salesforce Managed Master Secret (which rotates automatically with each major release) and a Customer Managed Tenant Secret.' (p. 63). If the customer manages its own tenant secret, 'Key generated by your company' also applies.

3.1.6.quote: Privacy Center is an add-on suite of tools built natively into the Salesforce platform ... It includes features around data minimization, anonymization/de-identification, supporting Data Subject Access Requests
3.1.6.note: Anonymization is offered via the Privacy Center add-on product, per the report's service descriptions.

value: Production access via password plus enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA) (SOC 2 p. 54)
Network-based intrusion detection systems across endpoints, identities, and network devices (p. 61)
Weekly internal and external vulnerability scanning; at-least-monthly patching (p. 62)
Annual application security assessments (manual penetration tests) plus invite-only bug bounty program (pp. 61-62)
Encryption keys held in a secured vault and rotated per Salesforce security standards (p. 130)
Customer Data deleted/overwritten from production within 90 days after a 120-day inactive period, and from backups within 180 days, post-termination (p. 71)

quotes.quote: Access to production systems is achieved with password -based authentication, enforced via multi -factor authentication (MFA)
Network based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are placed across endpoints, identities, and network devices to monitor malicious activities on the network
Vulnerability scans are performed on both internal and external facing production systems ... at least weekly
ASAs are closed -box web application penetration tests, focused on manual penetration testing
encryption keys were maintained in a secured vault
it is securely overwritten or deleted from production within 90 days, and from backups within 180 days

3.2.1.quote: Production data centers are in the following locations: ... Amsterdam, Netherlands • Stockholm, Sweden • Paris, France • Frankfurt, Germany
3.2.1.note: EU production colocation data centers are listed (Amsterdam, Paris, Frankfurt; plus Stockholm in the EU). Whether EU hosting is used for a given tenant depends on the customer's instance/region.

absent_notes.3.1.7: The word 'pseudonymization' does not appear in the report. Privacy Center mentions 'anonymization/de-identification' (p. 27) but pseudonymization is not explicitly stated.
